Verify recoded category counts against the counts a release published

Source: R/categorical_guard.R
vrfmrg.Rd

Compares the number of rows per category after a recode with the counts the data source published for those categories (for example the frequency table in a codebook or a statistical release). If they disagree, it tries every reordering of the labels and names the one under which the observed counts would match, which is the signature of labels attached to the wrong groups. Use it after decoding or recoding a column whenever published totals exist.

Usage

vrfmrg(x, pub, tol = 0, strict = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A character or factor vector after recoding.

pub

Named numeric vector, label = published count.

tol

Non-negative number, default 0. The absolute difference in counts allowed per label, for releases that round or suppress small counts.

strict

Logical, default TRUE: a mismatch is an error, so a pipeline stops. FALSE returns the result with ok = FALSE, the permutation that would explain the counts and the message the error would have carried, for callers that want to report it or pass the permutation to rlblfrns.

Value

A list of class rmbl_margin_check (it prints as a box) with elements counts (named numeric, observed count per published label), published (named numeric), ok (logical), permutation (named character, true label = label it would have to be read as, or NULL) and message (character, or NULL when ok). It is returned invisibly when the counts match and visibly when strict = FALSE and they do not. With strict = TRUE a mismatch is an error instead.

Details

For each label \(l\) in names(published) the observed count is \(n_l = \sum_i 1[x_i = l]\) (missing values excluded). The counts match when \(|n_l - p_l| \le\) tol for every label.

On a mismatch, and when there are at most 7 labels, the function searches the \(k!\) permutations of the labels (5040 at \(k = 7\)) for the first non-identity one under which the observed counts match the published counts, and names it in the message. With more than 7 labels no search is done and permutation is NULL. Several permutations can match when counts are tied; only the first is reported.

A label that occurs in x but not in pub is always a failure (no permutation search). pub must be a named numeric vector, otherwise an error.

See also

xfrvrf, rlblfrns.

Examples

x <- c("White", "White", "Black", "Indigenous", "White", "Black")
vrfmrg(x, c(White = 3, Black = 2, Indigenous = 1))$ok
#> [1] TRUE

# swapped labels: the permutation that explains the counts is named
r <- vrfmrg(x, c(White = 2, Black = 3, Indigenous = 1),
                      strict = FALSE)
r$permutation
#>        White        Black   Indigenous 
#>      "Black"      "White" "Indigenous" 

# a release that rounds counts to the nearest 5
vrfmrg(rep(c("A", "B"), c(48, 21)), c(A = 50, B = 20),
                 tol = 2)$ok
#> [1] TRUE

# the default is to stop
try(vrfmrg(x, c(White = 2, Black = 3, Indigenous = 1)))
#> Error : vrfmrg: recoded counts do not match the published counts. White: observed 3, published 2; Black: observed 2, published 3; Indigenous: observed 1, published 1. The observed counts match the published ones if the labels are permuted (White -> Black, Black -> White): the labels are attached to the wrong groups.
